patterns: PageHeader → FilterBar → DataTable → Pagination, details in a Drawer
Production stage: PageHeader variant=frame with title, status, the journey Menu and actions on one line, no back
Page navigation: the TopBar trail only (breadcrumbs), e.g. Produções › <título> › <etapa>
Studio: AppShell bleed → WorkspaceLayout docked → Toolbar (SaveIndicator at the end) + Prose
Creation page: FixedFrame with form, live preview aside and action footer

must: Use only public exports from @content-ventures/design-system/v3 and /icons for visual UI
Search the Design System before composing product components; add missing pieces to the DS with a specimen and a test
Preserve structural component spacing and responsive behavior
Use DS Tooltip for every hint; style in-document markers through Prose data-* hooks and DS proseWidgets
Write UI copy in Brazilian Portuguese; buttons start with a verb
Navigate between pages only through the TopBar trail (breadcrumbs); every level but the current one is a link
avoid: Local visual primitives, tokens, fonts, icons, themes or substitute UI libraries
Local CSS modules, class names, inline styles, lowercase markup, DOM creation or editor node views
Adjacent open Section components inside PageStack
Decorative side borders or per-paragraph boxes
Filler copy: extra eyebrows, subtitles, hints or notices
Hover handlers that scroll the transcript
PageHeader back or any other page back link

decisions: João requires navigation always by breadcrumbs (October 16, 2026). The TopBar trail is the only page navigation: every production stage shows "Produções › <título da produção> › <etapa>" with every level but the current one a link, the title opening the stage the production is on, and deciders also starting at Produções. Overlays and drawers add no level. Nothing uses PageHeader back or a header back link; scripts/check-content-density.mjs rejects it. Recovery actions inside error and access states ("Ver produções") and in-flow steps ("Voltar às aprovações") stay. On phones the DS TopBar shows the first and the current level; Reporter adds no in-page breadcrumb.

The user requires R2 UI previews inside the existing workspace navigation alongside Início, Produções and Modelos, not in a separate prototype app. Enable only the demonstrative R2 navigation and screens; keep domain/worker release gates on R1 and all R2 interactions demonstrative. Preserve the shared header, account, breadcrumbs, command palette and admin-only CMS access. Review before integrating into existing production editors or delivery.

The user approved an editorial home inspired by the supplied content, video and course dashboards: one featured production with its real text, cover when available and next action; consistent recent-production cards; personal pending actions and stage counts on the right; visual carousel model previews. On phones, pending actions follow the featured production and model previews stay compact. Reuse public DS components, preserve permissions and period selection, and keep all work local.

The user chose worker-first prompt management: uniform large cards for Gerar artigo and Gerar carrossel open an ordered, read-only workflow with clickable prompt nodes and a side editor. The page header follows the selected worker; reload and activation actions belong inside the worker. Shared instructions remain inside worker details. Keep conditional execution, manual review boundaries and on-demand editing explicit. Use only public DS components; all changes stay local until remote actions are authorized.

The user requested more vertical breathing room only for the Modelos page's tabs and filter toolbar. Use the public DS FilterBar spacing=comfortable option, with --s-2 above and below the tab rail and aligned search/actions. Preserve horizontal tab spacing and compact carousel pickers. This preview depends on the unpublished local filter-bar-spacing DS change; publish and pin the DS through the approved workflow before any remote delivery.

Keep the R1 navigation within the approved transcript → article → approval → carousel → export scope. Hide the standalone Imagens, Banners and Citações destinations from the sidebar and command palette until their product scope is approved, without assigning a future release. Remove the article menu shortcut for creating a standalone banner. Preserve the existing production tools, role-based approvals, carousel models and the previously approved Logs, Prompts and Versões footer. All work remains local until the user explicitly authorizes a remote action.

The sidebar places Logs and Prompts in the bottom utilities area beside the product version history, now labelled Versões. Preserve role-based access, existing routes, command-palette grouping and the public Design System Sidebar composition.

The user requested a visible local test-profile selector at the bottom-left sidebar account area, with Editor, Aprovador and Admin. Reuse the public DS Select and preserve keyboard focus while switching. Keep the account unchanged, retain unsaved form state, persist selected permissions across requests/reloads/local tabs, and expose the same choices in immersive production actions. Local Aprovador covers article and carousel review; cloud accounts never expose this capability.

New production confirms Material and Pauta, then opens the existing article editor with one queued generation. Planning and evidence selection run automatically in the saved pipeline; show animated preparation inside the editor until the live preview arrives. Keep toolbar, stop/retry, source attribution and reload continuity. Old structure URLs redirect to the editor; a queue refusal preserves the saved production there.

Material preparation opens a responsive Design System progress dialog for pasted text, files and imported links. Keep typing uninterrupted, allow the dialog to close and reopen without stopping processing, and distinguish reading/uploading, audio transcription and metadata analysis. Display upload percentages only from confirmed transferred bytes; processing remains indeterminate. Preserve source input on failures, offer the appropriate retry, and briefly confirm readiness before returning to the material form.

Polish the approved six Seafood carousel variations as premium B2B editorial creatives: a consistent 84px safe margin, opt-in balanced/optically fitted headlines with explicit minimum font sizes, intentional photo crops, quieter folio/signature and typographic quotation marks. Increase library thumbnail sharpness and desktop comparison size; allow each page to open in a readable DS Dialog with previous/next and a return action. Preserve all model IDs, slot contracts, stored copy, source references and existing exports; keep legacy render defaults unchanged. Do not add decorative charts, statistics, invented quotes or a parallel app design system.

The user approved Seafood Brasil-inspired photo-led navy/blue/cyan carousel directions. Offer six editable variations in Notícia, Explica and Podcast through the existing DS library, creation selector and switch drawer. Keep legacy IDs/defaults and article text; show fit warnings. Demo image/copy are explicitly illustrative and never substituted into real outputs. Preserve studio chrome, use a typeset brand label until the official logo asset arrives, and never invent statistics, podcast quotes or Marketing approval.
The product shell uses the complete DS navigation pattern
The visible menu contains only routes available to the user in the current release; Logs shows only to admins
Studios use the full width with one line of chrome above the text
Every production stage shares one compact header line with the journey menu
Status colours are reserved for state; meters and sparklines are neutral by default
AI output carries the Simulação local label while the product runs on the local simulation
Reporter consumes DS 0.2.0 from the editorial-studio branch until the version is tagged and pinned

The user selected Pixabay for free commercial article and banner photography without obligatory published credits. Use horizontal originals of at least 2400 × 1350 pixels, seafood searches, optional editorial curation and uncropped previews. Identify reduced API previews honestly and require original-download access before importing; never upscale. Retain author, source and licence internally, show provider identification in the library, preserve legacy assets/licences and the approved Design System. Resolution and editorial awards do not guarantee relevance or aesthetic quality.
